_strings.@@2b3b2d4f1267: Personal Tax Credit (personal exemption credit) — Every Arkansas individual filer. One credit each for: yourself, spouse, and each dependent; plus extra credit boxes for age 65 or over (as of January 1, 2026), '65 Special' (age 65+ not claiming the retirement income exemption), blind, deaf, and head of household/surviving spouse. Listed in the Personal Tax Credits section of the return.
_strings.@@2cda7a80c76f: Additional Tax Credit for Qualified Individuals (low-income credit) — An individual taxpayer with net income up to $27,600 (2025, indexed from 2024's $26,900) who timely files an Arkansas income tax return (Act 1 of the Second Extraordinary Session of 2021). Doubled for joint Filing Status 2, and computed separately per spouse for Filing Status 4.

_strings.@@5134335aaefa: Credit for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities — Taxpayers who have a dependent (or self) who qualifies with a developmental disability, as certified on Form AR1000-DD (formerly AR1000RC5). Certifications valid on January 1, 2022 and all new certifications from that date forward have no expiration date; the AR1000TC must be submitted yearly, and the AR1000-DD attached the first year the credit is claimed. The credit follows the child (no matter who the caretaker is) and can only be claimed on one tax return per year.
_strings.@@627f1db6486a: Treaty conformity — AR does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by AR. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Arkansas does NOT conform to federal tax treaty exemptions. Two independent .gov-sourced facts establish this for 2025: (1) The AR1000F return does NOT start from federal adjusted gross income. It builds Arkansas income line-by-line from source documents — Line 8 W-2 wages, Line 10 interest, Line 11 dividends, etc., summed to Line 23 'Total Income' and then to Arkansas AGI on Line 25. Because income is captured from the W-2/source level, a federal treaty exclusion taken on the federal return does NOT carry through. (2) The 2025 instructions state explicitly (Line 22 income section, p.13-14): 'Foreign students who are exempt from federal taxes because of a tax treaty must file and pay tax on all income including non-qualified scholarship or fellowship income' and 'Stipends are taxable.' That is an affirmative requirement to tax treaty-exempt income, equivalent to a treaty add-back. Therefore treaty-exempt income IS re-taxed by Arkansas -> conforms_to_federal_treaties = false. (The 2025 wording is verbatim identical to the 2024 wording — re-read, not assumed.)
_strings.@@74e0e92430e9: If any of your income was exempt from federal tax under a treaty: AR does not conform to federal tax treaties, so that income is still taxable to AR — do not carry the federal exclusion onto the state return.

calls.work_head: AR state income tax (2025, graduated brackets): taxable_base $44,940.00 — which must be the state's OWN gross-income computation (never federal AGI) — for PA, the sum of the eight separately-computed PA income classes, where a loss in one class never offsets another — minus standard deduction [married_filing_jointly (qualifying surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column)] = $4,940 = $40,000.00; graduated tax on $40,000 [married_filing_jointly (qualifying surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column) schedule]: 0 x $5,599.00 (the $0-$5,599 bracket) = $0.00; 0.02 x $5,600.00 (the $5,599-$11,199 bracket) = $112.00; 0.03 x $4,800.00 (the $11,199-$15,999 bracket) = $144.00; 0.034 x $10,400.00 (the $15,999-$26,399 bracket) = $353.60; 0.039 x $13,601.00 (the $26,399+ bracket) = $530.44; total $1,140.04 -> $1,140

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: AR1000F Line 29: 'TAX: (Enter tax from tax table)' — the tax on Line 28 ('Subtract line 27 from line 25. This is your Net Taxable Income.'), per the 2025 AR1000F/AR1000NR Instructions, Tax Computation, Lines 26-29. This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply AR1000F Line 25, 'Adjusted Gross Income (AGI)' — Arkansas AGI, i.e. Line 23 Total Income (built line-by-line from source documents, Lines 8-22: W-2 wages, interest, dividends, etc.; Arkansas does NOT start from federal AGI or federal taxable income) minus Line 24 adjustments (Form AR1000ADJ). The op subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (Line 27) to reach Line 28 Net Taxable Income and applies the brackets (the Line 29 tax). If you itemize (Form AR3), the shipped standard deduction is wrong for you — compute Line 27 on the form instead. Test-vector counts are zero by construction: Arkansas ships NO personal/dependent exemption keys (the $29-per-person amounts are CREDITS against tax, AR1000F Lines 7A/7B) — the engine refuses nonzero counts for this state by design. NO 2025 RATE CUT — the 3.9% top rate carries forward from 2024 unchanged. The 2025 booklet's Special Information for Tax Year 2025 states it verbatim: 'Individual Income Tax Rate Reduction (Act 1 of the Second Extraordinary Session of 2024) — Marginal Income Tax rates for 2025 are 3.9%, as amended in 2024.' What moved for 2025 is the annual INDEXING (Ark. Code Ann. 26-51-201(d)(1)): the 0% floor now runs to $5,599 (2024: $5,499), 2% to $11,199 (was $10,899), 3% to $15,999 (was $15,599), 3.4% to $26,399 (was $25,699), and 3.9% starts at $26,400 (was $25,700). Both the 2025 Indexed Tax Brackets PDF and the booklet's 2025 tax tables print the same schedule. Arkansas has ONE bracket schedule for every filing status — the published 2025 Indexed Tax Brackets and the tax tables do not vary by status, so all four statuses ship identical brackets. Filing Status 2 (married filing joint) runs the couple's COMBINED Line 28 net taxable income through the same un-widened schedule; Arkansas instead offers Filing Status 4 (married filing separately on the SAME return), where each spouse's own Line 28 income goes through the schedule in a separate column (tax = Line 29 column A + column B, summed on Line 30) — often less total tax than status 2. This op models a single run of one income through the schedule. Surviving Spouse is a SEPARATE Arkansas status (Filing Status 6) with a $2,470 standard deduction — NOT the $4,940 married-filing-joint amount. The engine maps qualifying surviving spouse to married_filing_jointly, which would wrongly apply $4,940; an Arkansas surviving spouse gets $2,470 (compute as single for the deduction). Table mandate at ALL income levels: AR1000F Line 29 takes the tax from the 2025 tax tables (booklet pp.24-30), which are computed at the MIDPOINT of each income band and rounded to the whole dollar — 'If you use a formula to calculate Arkansas income tax, the results must match the table exactly. The calculations in the table are made at the midpoint of each income level' (2025 Indexed Tax Brackets; worked examples: $75,900-$76,000 band -> $75,950 x .039 = $2,962.05 - $419.96 = $2,542.09 -> $2,542; $14,800-$14,900 band -> $14,850 x .030 = $445.50 - $223.97 = $221.53 -> $222). Bracket math may differ from the table by a few dollars within a band; the filed form must use the table. CRITICAL — shipped brackets are exact ONLY for net taxable income up to $94,700 (2024's boundary was $92,300). From $94,701 to $97,800 the official 2025 schedule phases the 3.9% bracket's 'minus adjustment' down from $419.96 to $99.30 (first step to $399.30 at $94,701, then $10 per $100 band), and at $97,801 and over the tax is 3.9% x net taxable income - $89.30. The shipped bracket math (equivalent to 3.9% x income - $419.96) UNDERSTATES the true tax above $94,700 — by $330.66 once net taxable income reaches $97,801 — so above $94,700 compute from the official schedule/table, not from these brackets. The Regular Income Tax Table's printed top rule — 'For $100,001 and over, your tax is $3,809 + 3.9% of the excess over $100,000' (booklet p.30, Rev 09/29/2025) — equals 3.9% x income - $91.00, while the 2025 Indexed Tax Brackets constant for $97,801+ is $89.30 (3.9% x $100,000 - $89.30 = $3,810.70): a $1.70 divergence, because $3,809 is the midpoint-rounded last table row ($99,901-$100,001: $99,951 x .039 - $89.30 = $3,808.789 -> $3,809). The filed form follows the printed table/formula. The published 'minus adjustment' constants equal the cumulative sum of the prior brackets to within half a cent ($111.98 = 2% x $5,599 exactly; $223.97 exactly; $287.97 vs exact $287.966; $419.96 vs exact $419.961) — no material rounding divergence, so the shipped marginal brackets reproduce the official formula to within one cent below $94,701. The phase-down region was independently checked against the printed table: the $94,901-$95,001 row prints $3,324 ($94,951 x .039 - $379.30 = $3,323.789) and the $95,401-$95,501 row prints $3,393 ($95,451 x .039 - $329.30 = $3,393.289), both matching the phase-down constants exactly. EXEMPTIONS ARE CREDITS IN ARKANSAS — none are shipped: Arkansas has no personal or dependent exemption that reduces income. It gives $29-per-person PERSONAL TAX CREDITS instead (AR1000F Line 7A boxes: yourself, spouse, 65 or over as of January 1, 2026, '65 Special', blind, deaf, head-of-household/surviving-spouse; Line 7B: $29 per dependent; totaled on Line 7C and subtracted from TAX on Line 34). These credits are not modeled by this op. Other nonrefundable credits reduce the computed tax on the form but are NOT modeled: the 'Additional Tax Credit for Qualified Individuals' (up to $60 per individual, 2025 net taxable income up to $27,600 — worksheet p.21: $60 at $0-$26,500 declining $5 per $100 band to $5 at $27,501-$27,600), the 20%-of-federal-computation Child and Dependent Care Credit (2025 AR2441 line 10 'Multiply line 9 by .20'), the $50/$100 state political contributions credit, and the $500-per-dependent Developmental Disabilities credit (AR1000TC line 7). Low Income Tax Table (NOT modeled): full-year residents whose total income from all sources is within the limits may take tax from the 2025 Low Income Tax Table applied to Line 25 AGI with NO deduction on Line 27 ('CAUTION: If you qualify to use a Low-Income Tax Table, enter zero (0) on line 27, column A. The Standard Deduction is already built into the table.'), which yields LESS tax than the shipped math at low incomes — tax is $0 up to $14,643 (single), $20,820 / $24,818 (HoH or Surviving Spouse with 1-or-no / 2-or-more dependents), $24,695 / $29,722 (MFJ with 1-or-no / 2-or-more dependents), and the tables are usable up to AGI of $17,500 (single), $25,300 / $29,000 (HoH/SS), $29,000 / $36,100 (MFJ). Married couples must file Status 2 to qualify; filers using the military-compensation, military-retirement, or employment-related pension exemptions do not qualify; itemizers must use the Regular Income Tax Table. Standard-deduction gates not modeled: the deduction is capped at income ('If the amount on line 25 is less than the Standard Deduction, enter the amount from line 25 on line 27' — consistent with the engine's max(0, ...)); the $2,470 Standard Deduction 'does not apply to taxpayer's dependent(s)'; itemizers use Form AR3 on Line 27 instead; and for Filing Status 4 or 5, if one spouse itemizes both must itemize (status 5 prorates deductions by both spouses' incomes). Amounts not part of Line 29 bracket math are not modeled: Line 31 lump-sum distribution averaging (Form AR1000TD) and Line 32 additional 10%-of-federal tax on early IRA/employer-plan distributions and Coverdell distributions (federal Form 5329) are ADDED to reach Line 33 total tax on the form. 2025 FORM RENUMBERING (payments side only): Arkansas withholding is now reported on two lines — 39A for W-2/W-2G withholding and 39B for 1099-R/1099-PT/AR-K1 withholding. The tax-computation and credit lines this op cites (27, 28, 29, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38) keep their 2024 numbers. Round all amounts to the nearest whole dollar on the return (2025 booklet: 'Round all amounts to the nearest dollar. For example, if your Form W-2 shows $10,897.50, round to $10,898. If your Form W-2 shows $10,897.49, round to $10,897.') — half-up, matching the engine.
